correctness.rationale: For generic input triples, implicit differentiation of the strictly convex p-loss yields nonnegative weights with sum one. When p>2, signed residual stationarity and concavity of the exponent (p-2)/(p-1) prove each Jacobian weight <=1/2. A single-step input response contains at most the transition 0,r,1-ell,1: it is monotone for p>2 and has at most three unit jumps for p<2. In the quadratic case the weights are 1/3 and exact finite-length counts follow. Step-vector decomposition and generic-line integration prove the global bound for every pair. Explicit reflection-symmetric triples and the scalar equation (delta-a)^(p-1)=(1+a)^(p-1)-(1-a)^(p-1) yield limits a/delta ->1,1/3,0, proving sharpness in each range. The standalone checker passed 4,480 random pairs and 24 constructed limits. Non-differentiable triples are handled by generic perturbations and continuity; finite tests do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The exact all-exponent sliding-three-point finite-path variation coefficient was not found in the inspected primary sources or published indexed neighboring results. Their assertions concern either foundational definitions and PDE mean-value schemes, cyclic/window medians, or a star graph with complete-pair Gini variation. These do not imply the piecewise sharp coefficient or its simultaneously sharp transition. Priority remains qualified: unindexed equivalent work could exist; search absence alone does not establish novelty.

value.rationale: The natural p-mean is used in nonlinear numerical averaging, but sup-norm stability alone cannot quantify input-perturbation variation. The theorem resolves every finite path length for three-point windows, gives a discontinuous factor-three jump from quadratic to subquadratic p-loss, and identifies the structural one-half Jacobian-weight threshold responsible for superquadratic nonexpansivity. It is neither a renaming of a standard median result nor an arbitrary sample computation. The restriction to unweighted windows of width three and absence of an independent audit are explicit.
